sections.label: Digital Government Transactions and Support
sections.summary: About 99% of Government transactions are completed digitally, enabling automatic support like U-Save rebates, CDC vouchers, Workfare top-ups and Majulah package.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: About 99% of Government transactions with citizens and businesses are now completed digitally from start to end, enabled by data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Singaporean households automatically qualify for and receive support like U-Save rebates, our favourite Community Development Council (CDC) vouchers and Child LifeSG credits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Lower-income workers automatically receive salary top-ups from the Workfare Income Supplement Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: And for our seniors, the Majulah package supports their healthcare and retirement, and the Senior Employment Credit supports their employment at the workplace.

sections.label: PSGA Data Sharing Safeguards
sections.summary: Under the amended PSGA, public agencies may share data with trusted external partners only when three safeguards are met.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Under the amended PSGA, public agencies are allowed to share data with trusted external partners only when three safeguards are met.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: These are: (a) having a legitimate purpose for sharing; (b) the arrangement is specifically authorised by a Minister or the Minister's delegate; and (c) the external partner is bound by clear contractual terms of use, including data protection and security requirements.

sections.label: Capability Support and Criminal Offences
sections.summary: The Government will work with partners needing capability support, and the Bill introduces criminal offences for individuals in external organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Where partners, especially smaller organisations, need to strengthen capabilities to meet these requirements, we will work with them so that safeguards are consistently applied.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: So, this Bill introduces criminal offences for individuals in external organisations.

sections.label: Equal Penalties for External Individuals
sections.summary: Individuals in external organisations face the same penalties as public officers for misusing shared data under the expanded PSGA offences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: With these expanded PSGA offences, individuals in external organisations face the same level of penalties that public officers are currently subject to for misusing shared data.

sections.label: Health Information Bill Framework
sections.summary: The Government will introduce a Health Information Bill setting out a framework governing information contributed to and accessed from the NEHR.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: The Government will also be introducing a Health Information Bill (HIB), which will set out a framework governing information contributed to and accessed from the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR).

sections.label: Cybersecurity Terms and MHA Exception
sections.summary: Cybersecurity and data security safeguards matching the HIB will be required through Terms of Use for external partners, with one exception for MHA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: Cybersecurity and data security safeguards matching those under the HIB will be required through the Terms of Use for external partners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: There is one exception relating to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

sections.label: NEHR data shared under PSGA
sections.summary: NEHR information for such assessments would be shared under the PSGA for public safety reasons.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: NEHR information for such assessments would be shared under the PSGA for public safety reasons.

sections.label: Amendments enable support for vulnerable Singaporeans
sections.summary: The proposed amendments maintain commitment to protect data while enabling vulnerable Singaporeans to receive faster, targeted and more coordinated support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: With the proposed amendments, we maintain our commitment to protect data, while addressing the reality that effective service delivery requires trusted partnerships beyond public agencies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Ms Jasmin Lau) (for the Minister of State for Digital Development and Information)
sentences.text: These amendments will enable vulnerable Singaporeans to receive faster, targeted and more coordinated support, when they need it most.

sections.label: Debate on oversight and data sharing
sections.summary: The debate centred on balancing central oversight with Statutory Board autonomy, whole-of-Government coordination, legal basis for data sharing and consistent governance standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Much of that debate centred on how to strike the right balance between central oversight and the operational autonomy of Statutory Boards; how to enable effective whole-of-Government coordination; how to provide a clear legal basis for data sharing across agencies; and how to apply governance standards consistently across public bodies.

sections.label: Bill extends PSGA data sharing
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to extend the PSGA's benefits by enabling trusted data sharing with external partners.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Singaporeans recognise the significant benefits that the PSGA has delivered within Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to extend those benefits by enabling trusted data sharing with external partners.

sections.label: Thresholds before data leave public sector
sections.summary: It asks what thresholds, principles and public-interest considerations must be met before data move beyond the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: What thresholds, what principles and public-interest considerations must be met before data move beyond the public sector?

sections.label: GPC recognises many data types
sections.summary: The GPC recognises there are many types of data, from anonymised and aggregated to business, economic and sensitive data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In our deliberations, the GPC recognises that there are many types of data; ranging from anonymised and aggregated data, to business and economic, and sensitive data relating to personal data and critical infrastructure.

sections.label: Bill extends data sharing externally
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to extend benefits through data sharing with organisations outside the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Henry Kwek will address this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to extend those benefits through data sharing with external partners, namely organisations outside the public sector.

sections.label: Standards for external partners
sections.summary: It asks what equivalent standards will be required of external partners as data sharing is extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As we extend data sharing to external partners, what equivalent standards will be required of them?

sections.label: Differentiated data standards
sections.summary: It asks whether standards can differ based on the classification and sensitivity of data shared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Can there be differentiated standards based on the classification and sensitivity of data shared?

sections.label: Assurance beyond self-declaration
sections.summary: It states assurance cannot rest solely on self-declaration, especially for sensitive data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: Assurance cannot rest solely on self-declaration, especially when dealing with sensitive data.

sections.label: Clarifications on external data sharing
sections.summary: It seeks clarification on funding, retention, deletion, responsibility and resourcing for external partners sharing data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: In this regard, I seek clarification on whether the Government would consider providing support through targeted funding or capability-building programmes to help such partners strengthen their digital resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: As we approach the Budget period, this may be a timely area for consideration, ensuring that trust and inclusion advance together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: I seek clarification on how long external partners may retain this data shared, how proper care, retention and eventual secure deletion of data would be enforced, whether responsibility for ensuring data wiping rests with the individual Ministries or centrally and whether Ministries are adequately resourced to manage these audit trails over time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: The question before us is how equivalence is assured, how compliance is enforced and how accountability is maintained when trust is delegated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Changi)
sentences.text: These clarifications are intended to ensure that we scale data sharing not just efficiently, but responsibly – delivering the best public good while safeguarding the data, privacy and trust of Singaporeans.

sections.label: Bill expands data sharing powers
sections.summary: The Bill moves from public-agency sharing to authorising data use, sharing with non-public persons and re-identification via Ministerial directions.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The Bill before us today moves us from a framework that, on the whole, allowed data to be shared between public agencies and subject to rules and regulations about such sharing and use, to one which expands the sharing of data expressly authorising: one, the use of data; two, the sharing of data with non-public sector persons; and three, even the re-identification of previously anonymised information – all through Ministerial directions and further authorisations, that is, data sharing and use directions given by a Minister.

sections.label: Data sharing and use directions
sections.summary: The Bill's amendments let Ministers issue data sharing and use directions and authorise sharing data with non-public sector persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments to this Bill, Ministers will be able to issue data sharing and use directions, and be allowed to further authorise sharing of data with non-public sector persons.

sections.label: Oversight of directions
sections.summary: The question asks what oversight mechanisms ensure a direction is not overly broad or made erroneously.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister thus clarify, what would be the oversight mechanisms to be applied in ensuring that a direction is not overly broad nor made erroneously?

sections.label: Commercially sensitive data consideration
sections.summary: The question asks whether and how data sharing and use directions require consideration of commercially sensitive data.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Could the Minister thus clarify about whether and how the proposed data sharing and use directions will explicitly require consideration and evaluation of data that could be commercially sensitive?

sections.label: Assessment factors for authorisation
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Minister must assess listed factors and whether they are documented in writing.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For instance, must the Minister assess the sensitivity classification of the data, the proportionality between privacy, intrusion and public benefit, whether less intrusive alternatives exist and the data recipients' security posture, and are these factors documented in writing for each authorisation?

sections.label: Re-identification, concerns, breaches, redress
sections.summary: The question asks about instances leading to re-identification, avenues to raise concerns, breach communication, and individual redress.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Can the Minister thus clarify: one, what instances would lead to re-identification; two, what avenues exists to raise concerns; three, how will breaches by non-public sector persons be communicated, particularly to affected citizens; and four, how can individuals seek redress in this system that has an increasing number of third-party partners or contractors?

sections.label: Strengthening governance of expanded powers
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to consider Parliament updates, clearer recourse for Singaporeans, and safeguarding sensitive information.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, I hope that as we expand the executive's discretion about the use of our data out of necessity, we strengthen rather than dilute the governance framework around these increased powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Thus, could the Minister consider, first, how Parliament can be kept updated and meaningfully informed about the use of these powers.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Second, how Singaporeans can have clearer avenues for recourse.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And finally, how can commercial and personal sensitive information be more explicitly safeguarded, even if the use and sharing of such data is subject to Ministerial discretion.

sections.label: Data sharing tied to purposes
sections.summary: The amendment Bill requires any data sharing with external partners to remain tied to the seven public interest purposes in the PSGA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under the amendment Bill, any sharing of data with external partners must still be tied to the same seven public interest purposes set out in PSGA.

sections.label: Ministerial direction for external sharing
sections.summary: The amendment Bill requires any sharing with external partners to be backed by a Ministerial direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under the amendment Bill, any sharing with external partners must be backed by a Ministerial direction.

sections.label: Penalties for external partners
sections.summary: The Bill holds external partners receiving public sector data to the same criminal penalties as public officers for misuse, with fines up to $5,000, imprisonment up to two years, or both.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The amendment Bill addresses the gap without adding unnecessary compliance burdens for partners, requiring external partners who receive public sector data to be held to the same criminal penalties as public officers if they misuse it, whether through unauthorised disclosure, improper use or re-identifying anonymised information without approval.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: These offences carry the same penalties already set out in the PSGA, which are fines of up to $5,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

sections.label: Risk-based data security approach
sections.summary: The speaker suggests agencies adopt a risk-based approach, with deeper technical assessments for higher-risk data flows and a lighter touch for lower-risk projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What I am suggesting is not imposing additional burdens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: But I suggest that perhaps we consider not imposing a one‑size‑fits‑all data security burden – I believe the Minister of State did touch on this point – but perhaps that agencies could adopt a risk‑based approach that looks at higher‑risk data flows, undergoing deeper technical assessments, and at lower‑risk or time‑limited projects with a lighter touch.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Where appropriate, agencies can also recognise independent certifications or existing audits rather than duplicating effort.

sections.label: Intent of the PSGA
sections.summary: The intent of the PSGA is not to prevent the use of data but how to use it securely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, the intent of the PSGA is not to prevent the use of data but how to use it securely.

sections.label: Trust at the heart of the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker says the Bill's heart is a promise that Singaporeans' trust will be honoured when they share their information.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Because once a data breach happens, the damage is already done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must remember that at the heart of the Bill is a simple promise – that when Singaporeans share their information, that their trust will be honoured.

sections.label: Expedited COVID-19 Bill passage
sections.summary: The backlash led to the expedited passage in February 2021 of a Bill restricting access to seven serious offence categories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The backlash led to the expedited passage in February 2021 of the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment) Bill restricting access to seven serious offence categories.

sections.label: Data flow to private companies
sections.summary: Data can now flow to private companies, contractors and vendors, and a power to re-identify anonymised information is introduced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Data can now flow to private companies, contractors and vendors, and introduces a power to re-identify anonymised information.

sections.label: Citizen rights under Bill
sections.summary: Under this Bill, a citizen has no right to know when their data is shared with a private company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under this Bill, a citizen has no right to know when their data is shared with a private company, no mechanism to find out which companies hold their data and no way to ensure they benefit from the value that data creates.

sections.label: Call for formal public review
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister would commit to a formal public review within five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it not be better to commit to a review now, than to legislate in the possible crisis of confidence later?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, question three: would the Minister commit to a formal public review within five years, including the directions issued, the data shared and whether the safeguards have been adequate?

sections.label: TraceTogether and PSGA data governance
sections.summary: TraceTogether showed non-transparency about data sharing has costs, and the PSGA establishes the framework for data governance across public agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: TraceTogether taught us that non-transparency about data sharing has costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Transparency is what makes data sharing sustainable in the long term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, we will continue to ask for three commitments: a public register, a mechanism to track and report citizen benefit, and a formal review within five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And I have flagged two gaps in organisational accountability that should be addressed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The PSGA establishes the overarching framework for data governance across public agencies, including provisions for sharing health data beyond clinical care – for policy planning, service delivery and community outreach.

sections.label: Three layers of safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill provides three layers of safeguards for data sharing with external partners, including Ministerial authorisation and criminal penalties for misuse.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill provides three layers of safeguards for data sharing with external partners – Ministerial authorisation, terms of use which impose data protection requirements and criminal penalties for misuse.

sections.label: Health data sharing safeguards
sections.summary: Speaker notes the Bill requires individual consent and a Personal Data Protection Impact Assessment for such requests, with MOH oversight, and urges further commitments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I note that the Bill requires individual consent and a Personal Data Protection Impact Assessment for such requests, with MOH oversight.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But I urge the Government to go further – commit that such requests will be rare and exceptional, subject them to close scrutiny and independent review, and publish annual reports detailing the number and nature of such requests to ensure transparency and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To further enhance trust, I propose that the Government jointly maintain a public register of all use cases where health data has been shared under PSGA for non-health purposes.

sections.label: Bill strengthens government help delivery
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens the Government's ability to deliver help that is effective, timely and dignified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: At its core, this Bill strengthens the Government’s ability to deliver help that is effective, timely and dignified.

sections.label: Purpose limitation and data minimisation
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Government will ensure purpose limitation and data minimisation in data sharing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: How will the Government ensure purpose limitation and data minimisation is done, so that we share what is needed and not more than what is needed, and not longer than what is needed?

sections.label: Cybersecurity expectations for partners
sections.summary: The speaker asks about the Government's approach to cybersecurity expectations, baseline and higher standards, support, and fair assessment of responsibility after incidents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: With that in mind, I would like to ask the Minister of State the Government’s approach to setting cybersecurity expectations that are robust but also clear and workable across different partners?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: For example, what is the baseline standard for all partners and what higher standards must apply for more sensitive data and what support will be given to help partners meet these standards?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: And the next point, and an important point, if a serious incident happens despite reasonable safeguards by these partners, given how widespread cybersecurity breaches are globally, how will the Government assess responsibility in a way that is fair, firm and predictable so that our partners have clarity and confidence to work with us?

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As Minister of State Jasmin Lau shared, I note that in tandem with the HIB, the Public Service (Governance) Bill complements and allows the Government to deliver better social services to Singaporeans nationwide, by permitting public agencies to share and use data across agencies, as well as with non-public sector partners.

sections.label: Safeguards for non-public sector data
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify safeguards ensuring data shared with non-public sector organisations is safe from cyberattacks and breaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, I would like to ask the Minister to clarify what safeguards will be put in place to ensure that data shared with non-public sector organisations is safe from malicious third-party cyberattacks and data breaches.

sections.label: External partners maintaining safeguards
sections.summary: The speaker asks how external partners will be expected to keep up and maintain safeguards before receiving shared data from public agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As hackers use sophisticated techniques to evade detection, they lurk in networks to spy over the long term, to steal sensitive information or disrupt essential services, among other objectives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Therefore, my question is, how will external partners be expected to keep up and maintain safeguards, before they can receive shared data from public agencies?

sections.label: PDPA financial penalties
sections.summary: Under the PDPA, the Personal Data Protection Commission can impose financial penalties for intentional or negligent contraventions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For example, under the PDPA, the Personal Data Protection Commission can impose financial penalties against an organisation for intentional or negligent contraventions of PDPA.

sections.label: Bill addresses data sharing blind spot
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to address a blind spot by enabling responsible data sharing beyond the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: It is people, especially the vulnerable, who fall through the cracks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This Bill seeks to address that blind spot by enabling responsible data sharing beyond the public sector.

sections.label: Offences for unauthorised data disclosure
sections.summary: The Bill introduces offences for unauthorised disclosure of non-personal data by employees of external partners, with penalties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Bill introduces offences for unauthorised disclosure of non-personal data by employees of external partners, with penalties of up to $5,000 or two years' imprisonment.

sections.label: Megan Khung's death
sections.summary: Four-year-old Megan Khung did not die because no one cared.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Four-year-old Megan Khung did not die because no one cared.

sections.label: System saw parts, not whole
sections.summary: Each saw a part of the picture, but the system never saw clearly, early enough or as one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Each saw a part of the picture, but the system never saw clearly, early enough or as one.

sections.label: External partners must meet standards
sections.summary: PAP MPs stressed external partners must meet the same high standards as the Government, with public interest tests and oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Many PAP MPs today have rightly stressed that when data leaves the public sector, external partners must meet the same high standards as the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With clear public interest tests, stronger oversight and firm accountability, including how this Bill aligns with the HIB that is upcoming.

sections.label: Data use commitment
sections.summary: The commitment is to use data to protect and share data to connect, not to stigmatise or surveil.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: So, let us be clear about our commitment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We will use data to protect, not to stigmatise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We will share data to connect, not to surveil.

sections.label: Further authorisation for external sharing
sections.summary: A second layer of checks, further authorisation, is added for sharing with external partners, requiring deliberation and Minister sign off.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: What we are adding is a second layer of checks referred to as the "further authorisation" in the Bill for cases of sharing with external partners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Before data is shared with external partners, it must go through careful deliberation within the Public Service, culminating in a sign off by the Minister or his or her delegate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Each authorisation must clearly state the purpose for sharing the scope of data to be shared and the specific external parties receiving the data.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: To Mr Yip's question on the delegation of Minister's authorisation, delegation if done, will only be to the senior leadership level of the Public Service.

sections.label: Anonymised data for external partners
sections.summary: Where identifiable personal data is not needed, anonymised data will be provided to external partners instead.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: The starting point is this: where identifiable personal data is not needed, anonymised data will be provided to external partners instead.

sections.label: Health information employment insurance rules
sections.summary: Health information used for employment and insurance purposes has additional requirements to seek consent and conduct a data protection impact assessment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: In the instance of health information, which Dr Choo had asked about, for health information that is used for employment and insurance purposes in particular, there will be additional requirements under the Public Service's rules to seek consent and to conduct a personal data protection impact assessment under the PSGA.

sections.label: Tiering cybersecurity requirements
sections.summary: Tiering cybersecurity requirements so smaller entities face less stringent standards is not advisable.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: While well-intentioned, tiering cybersecurity requirements so that smaller entities face less stringent standards is not advisable.

sections.label: PDPC financial penalties
sections.summary: The Personal Data Protection Commission can impose financial penalties on organisations for intentional or negligent contraventions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: The Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) can impose financial penalties on organisations for intentional or negligent contraventions.

sections.label: Penalties aligned with PDPA and PSGA
sections.summary: Penalties are aligned with current PDPA offences for external partners and PSGA offences for public officials.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: The penalties are aligned with current PDPA offences for external partners and PSGA offences for public officials.

sections.label: Liability assessed in context
sections.summary: Liability is assessed by looking at all facts and circumstances, including the incident's nature, safeguards, and parties' actions and response.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Liability is assessed in context: we look at all of the facts and the circumstances, and we consider the nature of the incident, whether reasonable safeguards were in place, and the actions of the parties involved, including their response to the incident.

sections.label: Parliament restricted TraceTogether data use
sections.summary: Parliament passed the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment) Bill to restrict the use of TraceTogether data to serious offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Parliament subsequently passed the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures) (Amendment) Bill to restrict the use of TraceTogether data to serious offences.

sections.label: Opting out causes incomplete data
sections.summary: Allowing individuals to opt out would lead to incomplete data, fundamentally undermining planning, policy formulation and service delivery.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: Allowing individuals to opt out would lead to incomplete data, which will fundamentally undermine our ability to plan, formulate policies and deliver services.

sections.label: Australia principle and existing PDPA
sections.summary: Australia does it as a sound legislative principle, and organisations misusing data face the existing PDPA and Terms of Use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: Australia does it, and I think it is quite a sound legislative principle. so, these are my supplementary questions for now.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: I spent quite a bit of time just now explaining how organisations will be liable if they misuse data: there is an existing PDPA, as well as Terms of Use.

sections.label: Public register and PSGA objectives
sections.summary: The public register will be considered as experience with the Bill grows, and the PSGA only allows data sharing for Public Service objectives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: On the point about public register, I think I mentioned in my speech, that we will consider what is possible, what is feasible, as we get more experience with the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: The reason why I said that the Member may have misunderstood was that the point raised earlier was about whether our citizens will benefit from the data sharing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: I needed to clarify that the PSGA only allows for data sharing for Public Service objectives.

sections.label: Five-year review period request
sections.summary: A Member asks the Minister of State to respond on the five-year review period point and says the Government will review what is feasible as experience with the Bill grows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: And second of all, could the Minister of State respond on my five-year review period point, please.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
sentences.text: And I think on the second question, we have said that we will review what is feasible as we gain more experience with this Bill.
